issues.legal_issue: Convictions for conspiracy and related offenses cannot stand when the prosecution fails to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the alleged victim was defrauded.
material_facts: The alleged victim said she learned of the alleged deception shortly after the document was executed, but her early complaint did not identify the accused or state that she had not received the stated consideration.

The approver was the alleged victim’s trusted representative, admitted participating in the fraud for a share of the proceeds, and sought to become an approver about twenty months after the alleged offense.
The approver’s earlier statements to police were withheld from the defense, and his testimony lacked reliable corroboration on material aspects.
Despite knowing that the document purported to transfer her land, the alleged victim did not seek a civil declaration that it was obtained by fraud, and no explanation for that omission was given.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution did not establish beyond reasonable doubt that the alleged victim had been defrauded. The accused were entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt, and their convictions and sentences were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. An approver’s evidence requires careful scrutiny and corroboration, particularly where the witness admits betrayal for personal gain. The Court also treated the unexplained withholding of earlier police statements as supporting an adverse inference. The supplied judgment identifies no specific statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for these principles.

rule.if: appeal_from_criminal_convictions and alleged_fraud_is_the_basis_of_the_charges and (early_complaint_omits_accused_and_nonpayment or victim_does_not_seek_civil_protection) and approver_is_self_interested_and_late_to_cooperate and (approver_lacks_material_corroboration or prior_police_statements_are_withheld)

predicates.appeal_from_criminal_convictions: The case is an appeal from criminal convictions.
predicates.alleged_fraud_is_the_basis_of_the_charge: The prosecution charges depend on an allegation that the accused procured a document by deceiving its signer.
predicates.early_complaint_omits_accused_and_nonpay: The alleged victim’s early complaint does not identify the accused or say that the stated consideration was not paid.
predicates.victim_does_not_seek_civil_protection: The alleged victim does not seek civil relief to protect title to property said to have been transferred by fraud.
predicates.approver_is_self_interested_and_late_to_: A witness who admits participating in the alleged scheme for personal gain seeks approver status well after the alleged offense.
predicates.approver_lacks_material_corroboration: The approver’s account is not corroborated on material aspects of the prosecution case.
predicates.prior_police_statements_are_withheld: The prosecution does not provide the defense with the witness’s earlier police statements for use in testing the witness’s testimony.
predicates.accused_convictions_are_set_aside: The accused’s convictions are set aside.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns fraud-based charges and the specified weaknesses undermine the prosecution evidence, the accused’s convictions are set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A defense is entitled to use a prosecution witness’s earlier police statements to test the witness’s testimony, even when the prosecution does not rely on those statements.
material_facts: The approver had made several statements to police before seeking approver status.
The prosecution did not provide those statements to the defense because it did not intend to rely on them.
The defense was thereby deprived of the opportunity to use the statements to test the approver’s evidence in court.
issues.conclusion: The defense could not be denied access to the statements for cross-examination merely because the prosecution did not rely on them. Their withholding supported an adverse inference that they would have impaired the witness’s testimony.
issues.legal_principle: A defense may use a witness’s earlier police statements to test the witness’s evidence or confront the witness with an inconsistent earlier version, regardless of whether the prosecution proposes to rely on those statements. Withholding them can support an adverse inference; the supplied judgment identifies no specific statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial.
predicates.witness_made_earlier_police_statements: A prosecution witness made statements to police before giving evidence in court.
predicates.defense_sought_statements_to_test_witnes: The defense sought the earlier statements to test the witness’s evidence or confront the witness with an earlier version.
predicates.prosecution_withheld_statements_because_: The prosecution withheld the statements on the ground that it did not intend to rely on them.
predicates.defense_may_use_statements_to_test_witne: The defense may use the statements to test the witness, and withholding them supports an adverse inference.

issues.definition: When the defense seeks a prosecution witness’s earlier police statements to test the witness and the prosecution withholds them because it does not rely on them, the defense may use them and their withholding supports an adverse inference.
